segments.text: It's a community outreach project, in which we need to know your opinion about campus dogs.
Do you think they are good or bad and should we have dogs in our campus?
I think we can have dogs on our campus because of course it is the national heritage
but we can have very controlled and limited number
and it should be very controlled under organisations
or people who actually want them
because societally it also affects lot of people
and students who come here to study
Because not all are very comfortable with it
So do you have any personal experience because of dogs or you faced any problem with your friends?
I had my own personal experience and I met friends also
Because I have female friend and they've had certain experiences about that
If i share about my personal experience
Once, I remember I was coming back from ICC
Because it was an exam season
And there was an instance specially near my Bhawan
Especially Vivekanand Bhawan
There is this very large group of dogs that actually resides there
and it's like, I don't know a family or something.
And that was very initial time
when I was in second year at that point of time.
So I had not seen at least in campus
this amount of dogs together
and they all were fighting together basically.
There are Govind dogs
and there were Vivekanand dogs both fighting together
and the fight was majorly happening on the same route
which was linked to my Bhavan.
So I couldn't go from ICC to Vivekananda
and I actually asked guard to help me, please atleast help me cross that thing
And he was like it's still lonely but
I mean for guards because they have this you know
Laki with them yeah
So It is very easy for them to scare away dogs
But even that huge of a group
Even if they start barking at me
I couldn't scare them off
They won't be scared for me
So yeah
so
It actually took me a lot of time
I guess more than 30 minutes
I was just waiting and standing there like this.
That's a waste of your time during exams.
Yeah, exactly!
And basically...
There is a pass, ICD.
I had to go to sleep and the major problem was because in exam season we are awake at
midnight and you know, there were not single persons on that road.
It was only me if have to cross then I'll have to do it but I have to take a Govindwala
route properly and I didn't even know if I will encounter dogs there but usually there
So the safer route was in fact the one which was having dogs.
It was a major problem but after 30-40 minutes they shifted so I somehow passed with let's say 2-3 people were going
But it was not good experience
About your friends, we got to know from our hospital that dog bite is very big issue
Like daily 5-10 cases of dog bites are reported and it is also a huge health issue
Do you think that if something like this happens to you, your opinion will change?
I mean some people are very scared about it and the process also even if a dog bites we don't know if it will get us rabies or not
but each of us have to get through that series of injections which is painful also
and time consuming
and I mean its very worrying
yeah its expensive
so it is maybe 1500 rupees
15000 rupees
It is not a very good experience.
You are right.
And like in hostels also dogs are used, dustbin etc.
Hygiene issues are created.
Do you think safety of dogs or people should be prioritized?
Because our admin seems to be very much interested in the safety of dogs as much as we have conducted interviews
So what do you think should be prioritized?
Students or dogs?
Let's say if dogs are troubling us then what solution should we give them?
I mean, I particularly think it is a kind of symbiotic thing.
If you actually prioritize how dogs will be kept
It'll actually solve humans also
So basically if you can actually create
Let's say they are at least trying to create food spaces
Where they will be feeding spaces
But you can create restricted areas and
Atleast have them where they can actually be cared for
And there not roaming around
Because dogs usually keep on fighting amongst themselves
and they are randomly roaming, they don't even get to have food.
So if you actually care about them, then they won't have to do these things
And all of this is actually causing trouble for humans also
so it's basically a problem on both sides
If we solve one side, it will solve the other side
So what do you think as a campus should there be stricter rules imposed?
What actions should be taken by the campus?
I think first of all outside dogs shouldn't be allowed
Second of all, what do we say that I don't know but like they should be prevented that
Dogs should be vaccinated second thing which are already there and they should be sterilized so that
more dogs are not
It is not a more population of dog is increasing in the campus
And I think feeding spaces are trying to stick but stricter rules over that because I don't think so people are right now following those
If there is no feeding zone, do you think people should be fined for that?
Because dogs don't seem to stay in places where they are fed.
Yeah I mean if there's a rule imposed
You should have penalties for whatever reason
But you can have any penalty though
but this should be a penalty
if there's a rule made and somebody violates it
That's how the rule is enforced in particular areas
So yeah
Thank you so much
